properties.name: Jericho (Tell es-Sultan)
properties.location: West Bank / Jordan Valley, near modern Jericho
properties.hypothesis: Joshua 6: Israelites march around fortified Jericho; walls fall; city burned. John Garstang (1930s) dated City IV fiery destruction ~1400 BCE and linked it to the conquest.  Intifada halted the Italian–Palestinian season: Sapienza’s Tell es-Sultan team records that autumn 2000 fieldwork was interrupted by the severe political situation, with a forced field stop into the mid-2000s before cooperation digs returned—proof that Jericho’s trenches track geopolitics as well as stratigraphy.
properties.found: Major Bronze Age destruction with collapsed mudbrick, ash, and stored grain. Kenyon redated Garstang's City IV walls/destruction to end of Middle Bronze (~1550 BCE), with only sparse LB occupation—not a walled Late Bronze city matching a ~13th-c. conquest model.
properties.divergence: Mainstream view: Kenyon's MB end dating (supported by later 14C) means the famous destruction is too early for a Late Bronze 'conquest' horizon; no fortified city fitting ~1230 BCE. Minority (Wood et al.) revive Garstang ~1400 BCE pottery reading. Debate continues but Kenyon's stratigraphy dominates textbooks. Pattern (A): real place and real destruction; dating/interpretation overreach relative to popular conquest sync.
properties.sources: Garstang & Garstang, The Story of Jericho (1948); Kenyon, Digging Up Jericho (1957); Wood, BAR 16/2 (1990); Bruins & van der Plicht Radiocarbon 1995; NatGeo 'Fall of Jericho' summary; MDPI Religions 14/796 (2023 overview); K. properties.notes: Not 'no Jericho'—site is Tell es-Sultan. Contest is chronology and whether Joshua's narrative matches a specific destruction layer. Evidence type (A).

recent_updates.title: Durupınar 2026 radar survey and drilling (Contested, low)
recent_updates.text: A permitted 2026 field season led on the Turkish side by Prof. Cenker Atila (Sivas Cumhuriyet University), with the US group Noah’s Ark Scans, scanned the formation with ground-penetrating radar and resistivity and drilled cores to about 18–20 m. The university says 366 core samples went to Ankara Yıldırım Beyazıt University for carbon and dating tests. The US team says it hit mostly soil rather than solid bedrock and reads radar features as possible voids or corridors.
recent_updates.solidity: Low. Contested: not peer-reviewed; lab results pending
recent_updates.caveat: No peer-reviewed results. The “no bedrock” and “corridors” readings are claimed by the Durupınar team. Drilling and the drone work are partly crowdfunded by the advocacy group. One outlet credits Ağrı İbrahim Çeçen University instead of Sivas Cumhuriyet University; affiliation is unclear. The Durupınar Ark claim is disputed; geologists widely regard Durupınar, by the village of Üzengili near Doğubayazıt, as a natural formation. Status, Oct 15–17, 2026 symposium (hosted by Ağrı İbrahim Çeçen University): project head Prof. Cenker Atila (Sivas Cumhuriyet University, which leads the project) said about 20% of the radar data has been worked through, that corridor-like features, room-like voids and a three-layered formation have been noted, and that small burnt-wood fragments went to labs in Türkiye and France for species identification and carbon-14 dating. He said the features may be geological and that scientists must speak cautiously. No lab results have been published yet; a French radiocarbon result was expected in late October 2026. The symposium host likely explains why one outlet credited Ağrı İbrahim Çeçen University.

properties.location: NW Syria, ~55 km SW of Aleppo
properties.hypothesis: After palace archives found (1970s), Giovanni Pettinato announced tablet parallels to biblical patriarchs, Yahweh, Flood story, and Cities of the Plain (Sodom, Gomorrah, Zoar/Bela) per Gen 14. properties.name: Jerusalem — City of David 'palace of David' (Large Stone Structure)
properties.location: City of David ridge, Jerusalem
properties.hypothesis: 2 Sam 5: David takes Jerusalem; lives in a palace. Eilat Mazar announced Large Stone Structure as King David's palace guided by biblical topography.
properties.found: Massive stone structure and nearby Stepped Stone Structure; Iron Age pottery assemblages debated (10th vs 9th/later).
properties.divergence: Whether the building is 10th-c. royal Davidic palace remains sharply contested; alternative datings and functions proposed. Bible correctly focuses search on the southeastern hill; palace ID not settled. Pattern (A).
properties.sources: Finkelstein, Singer-Avitz, Herzog & Ussishkin (2007), Tel Aviv 34(2):142–164, https://doi.org/10.1179/tav.2007.2007.2.142; Mazar BAR articles on David's palace; Finkelstein et al. critiques in Tel Aviv / BAS; City of David excavation summaries; https://armstronginstitute.org/
properties.notes: Method case: using Bible as digging guide can work for neighborhoods and still overshoot on named rooms. Evidence type (A).
